title: experiment-batch-orchestration-for-llm-fallbacks-scratchpad
body:
Purpose
---
Quick working notes on how to orchestrate batched experiments that exercise LLM fallbacks and model-variant routing during canaries/A-Bs. Focus is operational choreography (who does what, what signals to watch, how to simulate failure modes) rather than evaluation math. This is a scratchpad — rough, opinionated, and deliberately tactical.

Context / why this exists
---
We repeatedly see subtle production regressions when new model variants or fallback policies are introduced (e.g., semantic drift in reranking, unexpected latency amplification when composite routing triggers). Existing canary docs focus on traffic slices and telemetry; gap: an operational playbook for batched experiments that exercise the entire fallback chain (primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> cached response -> simple heuristic fallback).

Goals (short)
---
- Provide a reproducible sequence to run a batched experiment that validates fallback correctness and safety.
- Define roles and handoffs so cross-functional teams can run canaries with minimal thrash.
- List observable signals, thresholds, and synthetic scenarios to prove graceful degradation.

Assumptions
---
- Customer-facing inference path supports model-variant routing and a pluggable fallback resolver.
- We have test harness to inject synthetic traffic and user-likeness (see linked artifacts).
- Oncall rotation and SRE alerting exist; we add experiment-specific channels and temporary thresholds.

Key definitions (short)
---
- Batch experiment: controlled run where a group of requests (by slice or time window) are intentionally routed through fallback/resolution logic to validate behavior.
- Fallback chain: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> prefix/KV cache -> deterministic heuristic/responder -> 503/soft-failure.
- Canary steward: the person responsible for execution and immediate decisions during the experiment window.

Roles & responsibilities (proposal)
---
- Canary Steward (product lead or rollout PM) — primary owner of the run, calls rollback, coordinates cross-team comms.
- Signal Analyst (data/observability) — sets up dashboards, runs quick analyses, interprets telemetry.
- Runtime Engineer (serving-runtime) — on hand for kernel/latency issues and inspects logs/traces.
- Model Owner (MLR) — ready to revert model/config if quality regressions observed.
- SRE/Oncall — monitors infra alerts and supports mitigation (scale up, change routing).
- Customer Success (optional) — standing by for high-risk customers in the cohort.

Preflight checklist (must clear before starting)
---
- Confirm canary slice definitions and traffic keys (cohort IDs, geos, endpoints).
- Synthetic traffic harness ready and smoke-tested (5–10k synthetic requests).
- Dashboards: latency P50/P90/P99, error rate (5xx), model-quality signal (eval score, top-1 rerank accuracy), hallucination probe score (from eval set).
- Temporary experiment alert rules created with quiet windows + escalation (documented in channel).
- Rollback playbook ready with automation (route back to primary, disable fallback policy).
- Communication stub: #rollouts-experiments, one-pager to execs and stakeholders.

Experiment choreography (step-by-step)
---
1) Pre-window: synth run + canary steward ack. Run synthetic workload and confirm baselines.
2) Window start (T0): flip routing for 1% traffic (control = existing routing). Set experiment tag in logs.
3) Observe initial 10 minutes: check for sharp latency / 5xx changes. If any infra alert > 5x baseline, immediate rollback.
4) Expand to 5% after 30m if stable. Run targeted evals on sampled responses (quality bump tests).
5) At 5% run 'fallback stress' burst: simulate primary model failures (GPU OOM, injected 503s) for 1 minute and observe fallback activation, correctness, and downstream latency.
6) Expansion to 20% only if fallback correctness metrics pass and no major infra signal.
7) If at any stage a quality metric drops below defined threshold, steward pauses and convenes decision call.

Signals & example thresholds (tunable)
---
- Infrastructure: 5xx rate > baseline * 3 for 5m => critical.
- Latency: P99 > baseline + 200ms for 10m => investigate.
- Quality: sampled eval score drop >= 6% absolute on prompt set => fail-fast.
- Hallucination probe: false-positives on key anchor prompts > 4% => pause.
- Fallback activation rate: when primary fails and fallback used, correctness pass-rate on sampled items must be >= 92%. If < 92% => rollback.

Sample telemetry queries (notes to signal analyst)
---
- Count by routeVariant and statuscode over time series.
- Latency Pctl by routeVariant and sequenceLength.
- Sample responses with diff between primary vs fallback outputs for same prompt keys.
- KV cache hit ratio and cache eviction rate (hot keys).

Simulated failure modes (to run during window)
---
- Slow GPU kernel: throttle primary model CPU/GPU for 30s to force timeouts.
- Bad model roll: inject a model that repeats/loops on test prompts.
- Cache poisoning: insert long prefix into cache and validate subsequent responses.
- Network partition: throttle egress to model storage to force fallback.

Experiment-specific automation snippets (todo)
---
- One-click rollback that adjusts routing policy and annotations for traceability.
- Auto sampling job to pull 500 recent responses and run eval harness overnight.
- Synthetic burst runner with weighted sampling to mimic real session lengths.

Decision matrix (quick reference)
---
- Green: infra stable, quality within +/-3% baseline, hallucination probe < 1% => continue expansion.
- Amber: transient latency bump or small quality dip (3–6%) => hold expansion, run deeper sample, increase monitoring.
- Red: infra alerts or quality drop >6% or fallback correctness < 92% => rollback and postmortem.

Postmortem template (minimal)
---
- What changed (model/config)
- Observed signals and timelines
- Root cause hypothesis
- Immediate remediation (what we did)
- Longer-term action items (owner + ETA)

Open questions / unresolved
---
- What is the right size for synthetic bursts to be representative? (Ethan to run sims with live traffic distribution)
- Should fallback correctness be measured via human-labeling for initial runs? Costly but higher fidelity.
- How to encode multi-variant comparisons into dashboards without exploding cardinality?

Notes & liveness
---
- This doc is a live scratchpad. If you run an experiment using this choreography, paste a short run summary below and add JIRA link.
- Quick run log template: date | steward | cohort | peak traffic % | notable signals | action taken | outcome.

Example quick run log (stub)
---
- 2026-02-10 | Marina | ecommerce-checkout-slice | 5% peak | P99 +120ms for 6m, fallback correctness 94% | held expansion, increased cache size | resumed after 90m

Immediate next steps (short)
---
- Ethan: run synthetic distribution experiments and produce a small report (due 2026-02-25).
- Jonah: add temporary grafana rows for fallback correctness and hallucination probe (ETA 48h).
- Marina: schedule dry-run with stakeholders and SRE (2026-02-22).

Slack/comms
---
Use channel: #rollouts-experiments for live runs. Create ephemeral thread for each experiment with pinned dashboard links and rollback command.

If you copy/paste this for a new experiment, replace the run-specific thresholds and keep the decision matrix rigid (so humans don’t arbitrarily escalate).

End of scratchpad.
